newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-URUGUAY, ARGENTINA RENEW BITTER RIVALRY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-URUGUAY, ARGENTINA RENEW BITTER RIVALRY.

text.p: Uruguay and Argentina renew one of international soccer's oldest and most bitter rivalries in Montevideo on Sunday when they meet in a World Cup qualifying match for the first time.

The stakes, always high when the old foes from either side of the River Plate come face to face, have been raised even further by the indiferrent form of the two teams in the South American World Cup qualifying group.
Only a few years ago both teams would have been expected to waltz nonchalantly through the nine-team group in which the top four qualify for World Cup finals.
But this time they find themselves slugging it out with the likes of Peru, Chile, Ecuador, Bolivia and Paraguay for a place in France and neither can afford any more slip-ups.

Argentina are third in the group but only three points separate them from eighth-placed Bolivia. Uruguay are level on points with their neighbours but two places below on goal difference -- which means they are currently out of the qualifying places.
Both sides are a massive eight points behind group leaders Colombia, who do not play on Sunday.
